subject: physics
stem: In Fig.1.1, two positive charges $q_2$ and $q_3$ fixed along the $y$ axis, exert a net electric force in the $+x$ direction on a charge $q_1$ fixed along the $x$ axis. If a positive charge $Q$ is added at $(x, 0)$, the force on $q_1$
options: shall increase along the positive $x$-axis.
shall decrease along the positive $x$-axis.
shall point along the negative $x$-axis.
shall increase but the direction changes because of the intersection of $Q$ with $q_2$ and $q_3$.

checks.notes: Transcription matches page; q1 is negative, Q attracts it toward +x so force increases along +x.

subject: physics
stem: Five charges $q_1$, $q_2$, $q_3$, $q_4$, and $q_5$ are fixed at their positions as shown in Fig. 1.4. $S$ is a Gaussian surface. The Gauss's law is given by $$\oint_S \mathbf{E}\cdot d\mathbf{s} = \frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}$$ Which of the following statements is correct?
options: $\mathbf{E}$ on the LHS of the above equation will have a contribution from $q_1$, $q_5$ and $q_3$ while $q$ on the RHS will have a contribution from $q_2$ and $q_4$ only.
$\mathbf{E}$ on the LHS of the above equation will have a contribution from all charges while $q$ on the RHS will have a contribution from $q_2$ and $q_4$ only.
$\mathbf{E}$ on the LHS of the above equation will have a contribution from all charges while $q$ on the RHS will have a contribution from $q_1$, $q_3$ and $q_5$ only.
Both $\mathbf{E}$ on the LHS and $q$ on the RHS will have contributions from $q_2$ and $q_4$ only.

subject: physics
stem: Figure 1.5 shows electric field lines in which an electric dipole $\mathbf{p}$ is placed as shown. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The dipole will not experience any force.
The dipole will experience a force towards right.
The dipole will experience a force towards left.
The dipole will experience a force upwards.

subject: physics
stem: A point charge $+q$, is placed at a distance $d$ from an isolated conducting plane. The field at a point P on the other side of the plane is
options: directed perpendicular to the plane and away from the plane.
directed perpendicular to the plane but towards the plane.
directed radially away from the point charge.
directed radially towards the point charge.

subject: physics
stem: A hemisphere is uniformly charged positively. The electric field at a point on a diameter away from the centre is directed
options: perpendicular to the diameter
parallel to the diameter
at an angle tilted towards the diameter
at an angle tilted away from the diameter.

checks.notes: Key image reads 1.7 (a) (official NCERT answer), transcription correct. But all charge lies on one side of the flat-face plane, so at an outside point on a diameter the field has radial and out-of-plane components; not perpendicular, tilted away from the diameter (d). Official key is likely idealised/wrong.
